1. `test_all.ts` — reading `process.argv.slice(2)` as the filter breaks `test_all.js` when invoked with other CLI args (e.g. existing CI/launch scripts that pass flags to `test_all.js` directly), and silently treats any stray argument as a test filter with no opt-in flag. Fix: use a dedicated flag (e.g. `--filter=<name>` or `--grep`) parsed explicitly, not "every positional arg is a filter," so unrelated args aren't misinterpreted.

2. `package.json` `test` / `test-only` scripts — switching to `sh -c '... "$@" ...' --` to forward args breaks on Windows where `sh` isn't guaranteed to be present/behave the same (this project supports Windows dev per CI config), and bakes a nontrivial amount of shell logic into a JSON script string that's hard to read/maintain and impossible to lint. Fix: move the arg-passing and grammar-skip logic into a small Node/TS script (or into `test_all.ts`/`test_runner.ts` directly) invoked from a plain `npm run` chain, so it's cross-platform and testable.

3. `test_runner.ts` glob pattern `**/*${testFilter}*.test.js` — `testFilter` is interpolated directly into a glob pattern without escaping glob metacharacters (`*`, `?`, `[`, `(`, etc.), so a filter containing those characters produces confusing or broken matches instead of a literal substring match. Fix: either escape glob-special characters before interpolating, or switch to filtering the full file list by plain substring match (`files.filter(f => f.includes(testFilter))`) rather than building a dynamic glob.

4. `test_runner.ts` filter semantics vs. AGENTS.md/PR description — the described feature is "run individual test files," but the implementation filters by substring over the whole relative path (including directory names), so e.g. `npm test debug` would match every test file under a `debug/` folder, not just a specific file; this is undocumented and may surprise users expecting Mocha-style `--grep` (by test title) vs. filename filtering. Fix: document the exact matching semantics in README/AGENTS.md and consider filename-only matching (basename) instead of full relative path to reduce accidental matches.

5. `test_runner.ts` "no matches found" path — it resolves successfully and the script exits 0 for a typo'd filter, which can mask a mistake (CI or a dev silently thinks tests passed when nothing ran). Fix: either return a non-zero/distinct result or at least log a clearly visible warning distinguishing "0 tests run, filter typo?" from "all tests passed," especially since this touches `test_all.js`'s overall exit-code logic across multiple bot runs.

6. Scope/interaction with `BOT` env var and the multi-suite `runAllTests` loop in `test_all.ts` — the filter is applied globally via one `DART_CODE_TEST_FILTER` env var across every `runTests(...)` call in `runAllTests`, including suites unrelated to the filter (flutter, debug, misc, etc.), each of which will redundantly download/launch VS Code and report "no matches" per suite. Fix: either short-circuit `runAllTests` to skip suites where the filter can't match, or document that users must also set `BOT=dart` (as shown in the examples) and clarify this is required, not just a convenience.

7. `package.json` `test-only` script — grammar-test skipping is decided by `[ $# -eq 0 ]` inside the `sh -c` for `test-only`, but `test` wraps `test-only` through another `sh -c "$@"` layer; args forwarding through two nested `npm run` + `sh -c "$@" --` hops is fragile (quoting of filters with spaces, e.g. "go to" two-word filters mentioned in the PR, is not verified) and not covered by any test. Fix: add verification (or at least a one-line note) that multi-word/space-containing filters survive both layers of `"$@"` forwarding intact.
